back: The resources used to produce goods and services: land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship.
Man-made resources used in production (tools, machines, buildings) and the money used to buy them.
The ability to combine the other factors, organise production and take the risk of running a business.
The skills and knowledge of workers, built through education and training.

front: Give the reward for each factor of production.
back: Land: rent. Labour: wages. Capital: interest. Entrepreneurship: profit.

front: Fixed or working capital: a sewing machine and the cloth?
back: The sewing machine is fixed capital (used repeatedly); the cloth is working capital (used up).

front: Name three ways government has widened access to factors of production.
back: Land redistribution; loans and funds for small enterprises (e.g. SMEDCO); vocational training and workspaces.

front: Why do many small businesses struggle to obtain capital?
back: Banks ask for collateral and charge high interest; many small entrepreneurs have no title deeds or savings.

front: Why does wider access to factors of production matter?
back: More people produce and earn, raising output and employment and reducing poverty and inequality.
